title: Extending Context Windows via Positional Interpolation
hook: Don't extrapolate to positions the model never saw - squeeze the position indices back inside the trained range, and a short fine-tune stretches the context window many times over.
key_points: Linearly down-scales input position indices to fit the originally trained context window, instead of extrapolating to unseen positions.
Extrapolation blows up attention scores; interpolation keeps positions in-distribution, with an error bound about 600x smaller.
Extends LLaMA context windows up to 32,768 tokens, demonstrated on models from 7B through 65B.
Needs only short fine-tuning, within 1,000 steps.
content_html: Shouyuan Chen, Sherman Wong, Liangjian Chen, and Yuandong Tian proposed Positional Interpolation in June 2023 as a simple way to extend a pretrained model's context window. The trick is to down-scale position indices so they land inside the range the model was trained on, rather than asking it to extrapolate to positions it has never seen.
extra_html:
How it works

When you push a model past its trained context length, the position indices run off into unseen territory, and the authors note this can make attention scores blow up. Instead, they linearly interpolate: the input position indices are scaled down to fit within the original trained window. Because interpolation keeps positions in-distribution, the authors report an error bound roughly 600x smaller than extrapolation. The method needs only a short fine-tune, within 1,000 steps, to adapt.

Why it matters

Chen and colleagues used Positional Interpolation to extend LLaMA context windows up to 32,768 tokens, demonstrated across models from 7B through 65B parameters. That turns a cheap fine-tune into a large jump in usable context, without retraining from scratch.
